terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. The tall slender Thai prang of the Wat Arun type. Deliberately a separate asset from the Khmer stone sanctuary even though both descend from the same Khmer tower form, and the registry notes say why: this one is tall, slim, pale and encrusted, where the Khmer original is squat, dark sandstone and ruined. A lichened stone terrace with a balustrade and one steep stair; a redented tower body with paired red pilaster strips in its re-entrant corners, a blind arched door under a pointed pediment on each face and a row of large arches at its top; seven receding tiers, each a ring of eight overlapping encrusted arches with plain rims, in a convex corn-cob taper; a domed cap and a tall gilt finial with a ball under the trident.

reasoning: Silhouette is the subject and it is complex: a CONVEX corn-cob taper of seven receding octagonal tiers, each wearing a ring of eight interleaved arches, over a redented tower over a stepped terrace, with a stair breaking the symmetry.
The redented plan is the reason a box decomposition is wrong here twice over -- it is a twenty-point polygon, and two crossed boxes would also z-fight along their whole intersection.
Repetition is four-fold and real: pilasters, false doors and pediments all repeat on the four faces and all three are InstancedMesh systems.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Three four-fold repetition systems and three merged multi-part components. Without the repetition systems the eight pilaster strips, four doors, four pediments and four door panels would be twenty draw calls of the twenty-four available, for four copies of three geometries.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: the CONVEX corn-cob taper -- seven tiers stepping in from the body and bulging before closing, not a straight cone
a ring of eight overlapping encrusted arches with plain rims on every tier, each reaching into the tier above, and a row of four over the body top
sixteen red strips, two on each re-entrant face of the four redented corners
a blind arched door on each of the four faces
a raised POINTED pediment frame rising from each door head
one steep flight cut into the +X face of the terrace, with raking cheeks
a low parapet ring on the upper platform, broken at the stair head
a 2.25 m gilt finial: stem, ball, and a trident with two CURLING outer prongs and a tapered centre spike
lichen and ground dirt darkening the lower plinth, fading out by 2.45 m

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: ONE stair, on the +X face. The plate shows one and the far side is unseen; real prangs often have four. Authored as one because that is what the evidence shows.

The porcelain encrustation is carried by a post-construction canvas tile of 1,400 chips per 3.2 m, not by the procedural texture set (which would discard every measured albedo). The chips are random within the tile; the plate composes them around each arch.

Each tier is a ring of EIGHT arches on an octagonal core -- one per face and one per corner at the same radius -- rather than the redented plan of the body. The plate shows the tiers as interleaved arches with no visible corner step, and an octagon puts every arch at one radius; a redented core would leave a 45-degree corner arch with 0.2 m of plan behind it and the rest floating.
The blind doors are authored identical on all four faces. A prang has one real cell and three blind doors; which face carries the real one is not observable here, so all four are blind.
Rear (-Z) elevation is unobserved. Authored as the symmetric repeat of the observed faces.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 9.00 x 18.00 x 9.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=32000 triangles, <=24 draw calls, <=16 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the tower, not with its stair treads.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: ONE stair, on the +X face. The plate shows one and the far side is unseen; real prangs often have four. Authored as one because that is what the evidence shows.

The porcelain encrustation is carried by a post-construction canvas tile of 1,400 chips per 3.2 m, not by the procedural texture set (which would discard every measured albedo). The chips are random within the tile; the plate composes them around each arch.

Each tier is a ring of EIGHT arches on an octagonal core -- one per face and one per corner at the same radius -- rather than the redented plan of the body. The plate shows the tiers as interleaved arches with no visible corner step, and an octagon puts every arch at one radius; a redented core would leave a 45-degree corner arch with 0.2 m of plan behind it and the rest floating.
The blind doors are authored identical on all four faces. A prang has one real cell and three blind doors; which face carries the real one is not observable here, so all four are blind.
Rear (-Z) elevation is unobserved. Authored as the symmetric repeat of the observed faces.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up. The prop is four-fold symmetric about Y in everything EXCEPT the stair, which occupies the +X face. That single asymmetry is why the stair had to be cut into the plan rather than added to it.

silhouette.description: A stepped stone platform to 3.15 m with a balustrade, a redented tower body to 10.20 m, seven receding arch-ringed tiers stepping IN from the body and bulging before closing to 15.20 m, a domed cap to 15.90 m and a 2.25 m finial to 18.00 m. The silhouette events are the terrace steps, the stair breaking one side, the tower's redented corners, the convex swell of the tier stack and the trident.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z both span -4.50..+4.50 = 9.00, set by the bottom terrace slab. y spans 0.00 to 18.00, the tip of the trident. The stair is the only asymmetric thing on the prop and it is cut INTO the terrace plan as a notch rather than hung off the outside: a flight projecting past a 9.00 m terrace would push the bounding box off-centre and over the declared width on one side, which is a real failure and not a rounding one. Cut in, the asymmetry costs nothing.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 2.201 : 1.243 against the declared 1 : 2.000 : 1.000. Area-weighted band comparison on this build gives mean |delta width| 0.008 and |delta depth| 0.013 of height with every band inside 0.03; three things it settled on the rebuild: the tier stack steps IN from the body (band 6 reference 0.193 against the body's 0.229, so the first tier ring is 1.55 + 0.30 of arch against a 2.10 body), the body-top arch row must be SHALLOW (a 0.30 m deep row read as a cornice at +0.030 in band 5), and the top tenth is finial alone (band 9 reference 0.017 wide -- the cap ends at 0.88 H and a 2.25 m finial carries the rest; the first build's 1.1 m finial also overshot 18.00 by 0.21). It was NOT close at first: built to the plate's apparent proportions, band 2 came out 0.170 of height too wide, the only band past the 0.12 flag in this batch. The plate is a three-quarter view from above and its foreshortening makes the platform look about a third of the prop's height; measured band by band, the reference puts the terrace top at 0.18 and shows nothing but tower across bands 2 to 5. The band table won and the terrace was rebuilt lower.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.70 rather than the 0.20 this kit gives an unseen elevation, because the tower and tiers are four-fold symmetric -- but lower than the chedi's 0.80, because the STAIR is not, and whether the real object has a second flight on the far side cannot be known from one view.

componentTree.name: Terrace, balustrade and stair
componentTree.topologyRationale: Three slabs, five balustrade runs, twelve treads and two raking cheeks are all the same stone, so all of them ride ONE component and ONE draw call. Grouping by MATERIAL rather than by location is the draw-call lever, and here it collapses twenty-two parts into a single submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Three notched slabs from y=0.00 to 2.45, a balustrade ring to 3.15 broken at the stair head, and a twelve-tread flight rising in the notch.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Three separate fixes. The balustrade's side runs carry the full depth and its front and back runs stop between them -- run to full width, every corner would put two outer faces in one plane facing one way. Each tread occupies only its own going rather than running back to the outer edge, so neighbours meet as opposed faces instead of twelve outer faces sharing a plane. And slabs meet top-to-bottom, which is an opposed butt. check-coplanar reports the prop clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is recorded as "extrude" because the slabs are extruded plans; the whole component is one merged BufferGeometry.

localFeatures.description: steep flight cut into the terrace plan
localFeatures.delivery: notchedSquare() plan plus merged treads and extruded cheeks

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the tower, not with its stair treads.

componentTree.name: Tower body
componentTree.topologyRationale: One extrusion of a closed redented plan. The redents are what a prang has instead of corners: the plan is a twenty-point polygon, so two crossed boxes are not a simplification of it but a different shape -- and they would z-fight along their whole intersection as well.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Redented square from y=2.45 to 10.20, half-width 2.10, redent 0.30.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: A single closed plan has no interior coincidence at all, which is the reason it is built this way rather than as crossed boxes.

blind arched door on each face
raised arched pediment above each door

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Porcelain-encrusted stucco, roughness 0.70, no texture set.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Corn-cob tiers and arch fields
componentTree.topologyRationale: Seven octagonal cores and sixty arch FIELDS (eight per tier, four over the body top) merged into one component and one draw call. They are merged rather than instanced because an instanced unit would stretch one tile's chips across arches of very different sizes. The apothem follows a cosine raised to 1.3, which keeps the taper CONVEX.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Seven octagonal tiers from y=10.20 to 15.20, apothem 1.55 down to 0.62, each carrying eight round-headed arch plates 1.05 of the octagon side wide, 1.38 of the tier tall and 0.22 m deep, sunk 0.05 into the core; four shallow (0.08 m) arches 3.30 wide over the body top from 9.55.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Each arch is sunk 50 mm into its core so back and core face are an opposed butt, not a shared plane; neighbouring arches meet at 45 degrees; the rim component's backs sit 20 mm further in than the fields' so no two backs share a plane. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.

localFeatures.description: ring of interleaved arches on each tier
localFeatures.delivery: archedPlate extrusions rotated to the eight octagon faces, merged

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME porcelain as the tower body -- one material, two components, because they are one surface treatment over two masses.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Arch rims
componentTree.topologyRationale: The sixty rims are one merged geometry in their own plain material: the border is what separates one arch from the next at distance, and it must NOT carry the chip tile.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.13 m border around every arch field, standing 0.08 m proud of it (0.06 on the body row).
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Back plane 20 mm inside the field's back; front plane 80 mm outside the field's front; the field's front face lies inside the rim's opening.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Domed cap
componentTree.topologyRationale: A surface of revolution closing the tier stack. One lathe of eleven profile points at 24 segments; the only round thing on an otherwise entirely rectilinear prop.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Closed lathe from y=15.00 to 15.90, radius 0.55 at the base to 0 on the axis.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Its base is sunk to 15.00, INSIDE the top tier, rather than resting on that tier's 15.20 top face. LatheGeometry is open at the bottom and an open rim sitting exactly on a surface is a seam the turntable gate can read through.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Gilt trident finial
componentTree.topologyRationale: Its own component because it is its own material, and there is nothing to merge it with. Ten segments and three cylinders in one merged geometry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Collar, 0.84 m stem, ball, cross bar, 1.0 m tapered centre spike and two CURLING outer prongs, from y=15.75 to exactly 18.00.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Everything here is a solid intersecting another solid at an angle. Nothing is flush with anything.

localOverrides.evidence: The plate's lower plinth measures distinctly darker and greener than the upper platform. Delivered as a per-vertex TINT on the merged terrace geometry -- (0.82, 0.83, 0.80) at y=0 fading out by y=2.45 -- rather than as a second material, which would cost a draw call and a shader switch to say that the bottom of a platform is dirtier than the top.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-terrace (PBR confidence 0.796) on the plate's LIT terrace face, which is two surfaces: clean grey limestone #B8B2A6 (the low-saturation band of the lower courses at (330..520, 900..960)) under an ochre lichen #CBB793 that covers 62% of the front face at (300..480, 830..900). The lichen is BRIGHTER than the stone in red and green and a multiplier cannot brighten, so the material holds the per-channel ENVELOPE of the two, (203,183,166) #CBB7A6, and the weathering tile paints the clean stone as (0.906, 0.973, 1.0) of it and the lichen as (0.995, 0.978, 0.783).

This plate is NOT the shadowless lightbox the retail plates are: its +Z return sits in real shade and the same stone measures #80807E there. That difference is illumination, not material, and the harness relights the prop itself.

Textureless as DECLARED -- no procedural texture set, so this measurement is what the shader multiplies -- and carrying one post-construction Canvas 2D tile (512 px over 3.2 m, seeded, seamless, map and bumpMap at 0.04) assigned after material construction: ashlar coursing at 0.32 m courses and 0.80 m blocks with 4 cm joints at 0.60, blurred cloudy tonal drift, the lichen as blurred ochre drifts with 1-2 cm speck crust, grey grime washes fading DOWN the face at (0.70, 0.72, 0.75) -- measured (0.61, 0.67, 0.73) at #7C7B79, lifted because the shaded return renders near luma 120 and 120 x 0.61 is under the silhouette gate's backdrop at 58 -- and light pocking. Nothing hard-edged but the pits and the joints.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-tower (PBR confidence 0.860). The CLEAN stucco between the chips on the lit face at (400..470, 470..620) is #E9DFCF (low-saturation p60-100), held 1% under so the tile's white chips stay <= 1; the earlier #D7CDBB was the chips-and-grime INTEGRATED mean of the same face, which the tile now reproduces by painting them. The shaded return of the same surface measures #8A8579 -- illumination, not material. Rendered body face 160 against the plate's 199 on the same lit face, tier fields 190 against the plate's 152 before the chips were densified -- the tier probe is chip-dominated on the plate and was not on the tile.

Roughness 0.70 rather than the 0.88 the stone carries: glazed porcelain chips set in lime give this surface a visibly tighter response than plain render, which is the one way the encrustation survives into a textureless material.

Textureless as DECLARED, carrying one post-construction Canvas 2D tile shared with the door recess material: white ground, blurred tonal drift at 0.91, grey weathering washes fading down the face at (0.74, 0.75, 0.76) -- measured (0.71, 0.73, 0.72) at #A6A296, lifted 0.03 for the hole gate -- and the porcelain chips as 1,400 hard-edged 4-7 sided polygons of 2.5-8 cm radius per 3.2 m tile (~40% cover, the tier faces' 39%), three quarters of them in loose rosettes the way the plate clusters them. Chip tones are ratios of the clean stucco: white 0.99, blue (0.40, 0.48, 0.72), green (0.44, 0.62, 0.48), yellow (0.88, 0.76, 0.40), ochre (0.80, 0.56, 0.42); the plate's blue (46,55,72) and green (75,99,75) are LIFTED from (0.20, 0.25, 0.35) and (0.32, 0.44, 0.36) so that a 6 cm chip on the shaded flank does not print as a near-backdrop pixel. The tile is also the bumpMap at 0.05, so a chip stands proud of the lime it is set in.

evidence: Measured INSIDE the plate's own blind door (viewEvidence region-door, PBR confidence 0.860). Worth stating because it is counter-intuitive: this recess is NOT dark. repetitionSystems.name: Redent pilaster strips
repetitionSystems.rationale: SIXTEEN strips at four instances, two per re-entrant face. The unit geometry holds all four strips of a single redented corner and is placed at radius zero, so the four 90-degree rotations supply the four corners and the offsets are baked into the geometry -- which is how an eight-part system costs one geometry and one draw call.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each strip stands 0.07 m proud of the re-entrant face it sits on, so it overlaps that face rather than lying in it.

repetitionSystems.name: False doors and pediments
repetitionSystems.rationale: TWO features on four faces in ONE unit: the blind door low down and the raised arched pediment above it are the same material and repeat on the same schedule, so merging them into one instanced geometry costs one draw call for eight parts.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The frame is embedded into the tower face and stands proud of it, so it OVERLAPS the opening rather than meeting its reveal edge -- the rule that stops a frame putting four coincident reveal faces in the model. The arch is swept from angle 0 to PI, over the top of the circle: written the other way it runs under and leaves the head filled solid with its own seam fighting across it, which reads as a square door with a ghost arch drawn on it.

repetitionSystems.name: Blind door panels
repetitionSystems.rationale: The back of each blind door, in its own slightly warmer material. A second system rather than a second colour on the first, because InstancedMesh takes one material.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Stands 0.015 m PROUD of the tower face rather than flush with it, and sits 0.16 m behind the frame's front plane. The depth is the feature: a blind door is a concavity, and the plate's own recess is barely darker than the wall, so geometry rather than albedo is what has to carry it.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. Band table 0.008 / 0.013 of height against the reference; the tier arches the first build omitted are what moved every layer. 18,060/32,000 triangles, 9/24 draw calls, 6/16 materials, 9/32 unique geometries, 3 canvas textures at 4.0 MB.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Six components and three repetition systems: 9 of 24. The terrace alone folds twenty-two parts into one submission by grouping on MATERIAL, and the door system folds two different features into one instanced unit because they share a material and a placement schedule.

materials.note: porcelain covers the tower body, the tier stack, the cap AND the door frames -- four consumers, one material, because they are one surface treatment over several masses; the arch rims are a sixth, plain material because the border must not carry the chip tile. Six of sixteen materials, ten in hand: this prop is nowhere near its material ceiling and does not need to be.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 18,060 of 32,000: ~14,000 of it in the 120 arch extrusions (9 curve segments each, fields and rims), the rest in the redented plans, the terrace and the finial. The first build spent 3,624 and called the arches below the resolvable band; they are the tier stack's whole identity at any distance the silhouette is readable from, and the budget exists for exactly this.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Extrusions of closed plans, plus one lathe. The redented plan is a twenty-point polygon and the notched terrace plan an eight-point one; both are single closed shapes rather than crossed boxes, which is both the correct shape and the only construction with no interior coincidence. The tiers are octagonal prisms wearing extruded arch plates. Boxes appear only in the balustrade, the treads, the door panels and the trident.

Three InstancedMesh systems carry 28 of the prop's 170 discrete parts. The pilaster system is the extreme case: eight parts from four instances of a two-part unit placed at radius zero, so the rotations do the placing and the geometry does the offsetting.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless -- no five-canvas procedural set, no per-pixel JavaScript, and every measured albedo survives as the multiplicand -- and three of the six carry a post-construction Canvas 2D weathering tile bound as map and bumpMap: lichened coursed limestone on the terrace, washed stucco with the porcelain chip encrustation on the tower, tiers, cap, door frames and door recess, and worn red paint on the pilasters. Three textures at 512 px, 4.0 MB of VRAM, and the factory builds in ~75-140 ms. Two of the three surfaces carry marks BRIGHTER than their clean ground (lichen, worn-through stucco), so those materials hold the envelope and the clean surface is painted into the tile with one multiply fill.

risks.description: The porcelain chip encrustation is a repeating 3.2 m tile of random chips, not the plate's composed rosettes, and the chips are 5-16 cm where the plate's largest pieces reach 20 cm. The two darkest chip families are lifted above their measured ratio for the silhouette gate.
risks.mitigation: The tile is seeded and seamless with chips in loose clusters rather than an even scatter, and at the distance an 18 m tower is read from the clusters integrate to the plate's mottled cream. A 300-chip, 5-13 px first tile read as confetti and was replaced. Rendered face lumas stay above 85 on the shaded flank.

risks.description: The plate shows a small arch over each pilaster group at the body top; the body row here has face arches only.
risks.mitigation: Behind a 45-degree plate at a redented corner there is only 0.2 m of plan; a first attempt floated as an ear past the body and measured +0.030 in band 5. The four face arches carry the row.

risks.description: One stair, on +X. Real prangs often have four.
risks.mitigation: The plate shows one and the far side is unseen, so one is what the evidence supports. Recorded as an assumption rather than closed silently, and it is why the rear-view confidence is 0.70 rather than the chedi's 0.80.
